result:
Solution 2 is the only one I accept; Solutions 1 and 3 are contradicted by a lower bound on the dimension.

**Lower bound.** In characteristic 2, write elements of $\mathfrak{sp}_{2n}$ as $\begin{pmatrix} A & B \\ C & A^T \end{pmatrix}$ with $B, C$ symmetric. The diagonal entries of the $B$- and $C$-blocks of any bracket are $2(\cdots)=0$. So $\operatorname{Im}(\operatorname{ad} x)$ has codimension at least $2n$ in $\mathfrak{sp}_{2n}$, and every centralizer has dimension at least $2n$.

Project $\mathcal{C}_2(\mathfrak{sp}_{2n})$ onto the first factor. Every fiber has dimension at least $2n$, so
$$\dim \mathcal{C}_2(\mathfrak{sp}_{2n}) \ge (2n^2+n) + 2n = 2n^2+3n.$$

This already exceeds $2n^2+2n$ and $2n^2+2n+1$, so Solutions 1 and 3 are wrong. Solution 1 wrongly assumes the characteristic-0 formula $\dim\mathfrak{g}+\operatorname{rank}$ carries over. Solution 3 wrongly takes the minimal centralizer dimension to be $n+1$.

**Solution 2.** Its answer matches the lower bound, and it checks $n=1$ ($\mathfrak{sl}_2$ in characteristic 2 gives dimension 5). I did not verify independently that the generic centralizer dimension is exactly $2n$ for all $n$, nor that no other stratum contributes more. I am relying on my recollection that $2n^2+3n$ is the known result, so this acceptance rests on plausibility rather than a full proof.

VERDICT 1: REJECT
VERDICT 2: ACCEPT
VERDICT 3: REJECT
